text: The Medicines, doses and formulations page is now two pages. Medicines, doses and formulations keeps the forms and dose ranges of each medicine. A new Monitoring and related care page has blood tests and reviews, getting the timing of a blood test right, fertility, sexual function, PrEP, and hormones around surgery. The words have not changed; reference numbers on both pages have been renumbered. On the home page, a new drawing of a dispensing set has a pump that pours the guide ribbon, the heading above the four cards now reads "Guides", and the Trans card links to Monitoring and to Add-on therapies.
Hormones around surgery and the Resources page now link to TransHub's pages on each gender-affirming surgery and to the Trans Health SA practitioner directory.

Bicalutamide safety points added from the Australian product information: it can make warfarin work more strongly (closer INR blood tests), it can rarely make skin burn more easily in the sun, and, for clinicians, its CYP3A4 interactions. The TGA safety update for the lung warning (interstitial lung disease) is now listed as a second source.

PBS prices and the co-payment are now dated. Five page titles (Angeliq, Estalis, Femoston, Kliogest and Trisequens) now start with the generic name. Two brand comparisons were reworded to be neutral, and an unsourced claim about steadier levels was removed.
New page: Add-on therapies. Treatments for acne, scalp hair loss, periods that continue on testosterone and vaginal dryness now have their own page, moved from the doses guide.
New section on the doses guide: Hormones around surgery. It explains the clot risk with major surgery and why talking with your surgeon and prescriber early matters.
PrEP wording is clearer: Australian guidelines suggest anyone on hormones (including those with a vagina) should take PrEP every day, not only around the time of sex.
The sexual function section on oestrogen and blockers is reworded in plainer clinical language. The facts are the same.

The doses guide now explains testosterone PBS rules: why an Authority is needed, which injections are listed, the patches that were cancelled, and e-scripts. The testosterone medicine pages link to it.
The privacy page is rewritten to be shorter and more formal. It still covers everything we collect, who can see it and how to have it removed.
The contact email, gamsaenquiries@gmail.com, now appears on more pages. The feedback form is still the preferred way to reach us.
The five injection training documents are now version 2.4 and the PBS Authority wording card is version 1.5. The injection-site drawing matches the one on this site.
Every medicine page now has a dated “Available in Australia?” line, linked to the supply page.
The supply page now tracks triptorelin (Diphereline), isotretinoin and finasteride, and names each isotretinoin brand that is out of stock with its expected return date.
Zoladex is PBS-listed until 1 May 2027.
Pharmacists now post stock reports with a personal report key, sent after their first approved report. Published reports show stock facts only.
Patient sightings are now marked “Unverified”.
The injection SOP and training guide is now version 2.3: Figure 1 steps 5 and 6 match this site.
Each medicine page now has a Print or save as PDF button and a Read aloud button.
Added a safety note on bicalutamide: not a first choice, regular liver tests, and the new lung warning in its product information.
Added PrEP and hormones: no interaction, take PrEP every day, and keep up kidney tests, especially with spironolactone.
Added the 2026 standards of care view on oestradiol implants next to the earlier caution.
Added the 2026 standards of care view on hormones and clot risk around surgery.
New section on fertility before starting hormones: storing sperm or eggs is optional, may delay starting, and costs differ.
New section on sexual function on oestrogen and blockers, with the options in the 2026 standards of care.
New Getting care section: Medicare items, prescriber directories, surgery links, neurodivergence, and questions about testosterone scripts.
New About page: who runs the site, how pages are made and reviewed, corrections, complaints and an accessibility statement.
Reworded opening lines to remove ranking words and to give the main risk next to the benefits.
Corrected the backup line: the monthly backup is being set up and has not started yet.
Easy Read guides: long lines made shorter, one sentence per line, and pictures that match the words.
Injection training package: all five documents are now version 2.3, each with a document ID, an amendment table and a next review date (24 October 2027).
Treatment-room card: the landmark key now sits under its heading, and the card says to check the QR code for the current version.
PBS Authority wording card, version 1.4: new print fonts, a document ID and a next review date. The wording is the same.
Safety notes on medicine pages now show, such as when to call 000 and which medicines to tell your pharmacist about.
Safety wording on five medicine pages now matches the product information.
The PBS cost section is brought up to date with the current PBS listing.
A brand that carries its own premium is no longer listed as “No premium” (Spiractin, Doryx). Where every brand of a medicine carries a premium, the page says so.
The testosterone injection documents are now version 2.2, with one A4 layout and larger tick boxes. The PBS Authority wording card and the pharmacy visit checklist are version 1.3.
Observation after the long-acting testosterone injection is now at least 30 minutes.
Doses and blood test targets now follow the AusPATH 2026 standards of care. Where guidelines differ, the page says which one it follows.
New safety point from the medicine leaflets: testosterone taken with an SGLT-2 inhibitor (a diabetes, heart or kidney medicine) can raise the red blood cell count.
New safety point from the medicine leaflet: meningioma.
New safety points from the medicine leaflets: rare severe skin reactions, heart rhythm (QT) checks and mood changes.
Triptorelin is now on the PBS, but not for gender dysphoria under 18, so puberty blockers stay private scripts for young people.
The supply page now shows when limited medicines are expected back.
The patch diagram now places every spot where the leaflets say: the lower belly or the buttocks.
Depo-Ralovera is marked as no longer available in Australia. Depo-Provera is the injection.
TGA shortage alerts are now available as an RSS feed at gamsa.au/feed.xml.
“Need help now?” now lists SA Mental Health Triage (13 14 65) and 13YARN (13 92 76), with tap-to-call numbers.
